name: s2-dose
title: Fate vs uniform TNF dose (the dose study)
question: How does the fraction of cells alive at 24 h depend on a uniform TNF bath, held at a receptor occupancy or fading exponentially, at death clocks of 30, 60 and 120 min per unit, with NF-kB intact and knocked out?
hypothesis: None is tested here. The held baths give the dose curve, which is reported, not tested (decision 41). Each fading bath is matched to one distance-study cell and bolus size, with the same peak TNF and the same sensed dose (decisions 50 and 56), and is the dose side of E4's comparison, which the distance study's runs complete (decisions 53, 55 to 58).
objective: Run Study 1's population (Study 0's builder: one Lipniacki model shared by the fate networks, absorbing death, coupling every 30 s, 24 h) in 8 held baths (receptor occupancy 0.005 to 1, denser below 0.2) and 9 fading baths c0 exp(-lambda t), one per distance-study cell (100, 300 and 1000 um) and bolus size (1, 10 and 100 uM um^2), at 30, 60 and 120 min per unit, NF-kB intact and knocked out: 102 points of 1,890 cells each (7 batches of 270, seeds 1 to 1,890), every TNF node off at t = 0.

assumptions.text: Receptor occupancy is c / (c + Kd), Kd = 19 pM, treated as quasi-steady (decision 32). A fading bath's occupancy is updated at every 30 s coupling, as the field composite's dose-response Step does with the TNF at the cell.

NF-kB's trajectory depends only on the bath: the fate networks don't feed back into Lipniacki's model, and the knocked-out arm (kappa = 0) removes NF-kB from the fate network only. So every batch of a point has the same NF-kB, and a run with one fate network reproduces it; the summary checks both.

baseline.name: population
baseline.description: Study 1's population in a uniform bath (dose_study.py): one Lipniacki model and 270 fate networks per batch, coupling every 30 s, absorbing death, 24 h, every TNF node off at t = 0 (decision 49).

variants.name: fading-baths
variants.description: c(t) = c0 exp(-lambda t), turned into occupancy at every coupling; c0 is the matched cell's peak TNF and lambda gives the bath the cell's 24 h receptor occupancy-time (decisions 50 and 56; analysis/exposure-design/ring_exposure.json). Half-lives 6 to 181 min.

variants.name: nfkb-knockout
variants.description: kappa = 0: the fate network's NF-kB node never switches on.

model_settings.name: cells
model_settings.description: 1,890 cells per point, 7 batches of 270, seeds 1 to 1,890 (decision 40b); the distance study runs 1891 to 3780 (decision 57).

controls.negative: NF-kB knocked out: no cell can reach Survival, so every knocked-out cell alive at 24 h has reached no fate. It holds at all 51 knocked-out points (no_fate equals alive_cells).
controls.positive: Occupancy 1 at 30 min per unit kills every cell in both arms, as held, saturating TNF did in Study 1 at that clock.

readouts: Alive at 24 h: no death node (Apoptosis, NonACD) ever on (decision 41); as a count (alive_cells, what E4 tests) and a fraction.
The survival curve: the fraction alive at each hour, and the median time of first death.
Death mode: Apoptosis and NonACD on at 24 h (a cell can show both).
No fate: no fate node ever on in 24 h.
NF-kB's first nuclear peak: time and nuclear fraction.
falsifiability: The dose study tests no claim of its own. Its numbers would be wrong for E4 if a batch had been run with other settings than its point names; the summary refuses a point whose batches' NF-kB differs from a fresh run of its bath.
limitations: The death clock is unknown and swept at three values. Under held TNF cells are still dying at 24 h (up to 0.15 of them in the last 4 h at 120 min per unit), so the alive fraction at 24 h is not where the curve settles. Between occupancy 0.2 and 1 the held curve has only two more doses, 0.5 and 1, and at 120 min per unit most of its fall lies there. Occupancy 1 is not Study 1's condition: there every TNF node started on, here every one starts off and switches on at rate occ per unit. The summary's check proves each batch's bath, not its fate networks' settings. The study records NF-kB's first nuclear peak, not its period. The 714 batch files (89 MB) are not in the repository but on the release s2-dose-batches (s2-dose-parquet-runs.tar.gz), checked by parquet-runs.sha256; data/dose.json holds every point's counts, survival curve and NF-kB peak.
claim: Survival at 24 h falls with dose at every death clock and in both arms, and is higher the slower the clock: held occupancy 0.005 to 1 leaves 0.938 to 0 alive at 30 min per unit, 0.976 to 0.003 at 60 and 0.990 to 0.241 at 120 (NF-kB intact). NF-kB adds at most 0.103 to the alive fraction. The 54 matched fading baths leave 0.123 to 0.996 alive, 20 of them within 0.05 of everyone alive. E4 has no verdicts until the distance study runs.

findings.summary: Held baths, 1,890 cells per point. Alive at 24 h falls with occupancy at every clock and in both arms, and rises with the clock at every dose: 0.938 to 0 at 30 min per unit, 0.976 to 0.003 at 60, 0.990 to 0.241 at 120 (knocked out 0.933 to 0, 0.974 to 0.0005, 0.987 to 0.138), from occupancy 0.005 to 1. Per unit of occupancy it falls fastest between 0.005 and 0.02 at every clock; at 120 min per unit 0.52 of its 0.75 fall (intact) lies above 0.2. At occupancy 0.05 and 30 min per unit, 0.572 are alive. Cells with no fate are the majority up to occupancy 0.05 at 30 min per unit, 0.1 at 60 and 0.2 at 120.

Alive intact minus knocked out is never negative at a held dose and at most 0.047 at 30 min per unit, 0.069 at 60 and 0.103 at 120 (occupancy 1). In the fading baths it is at most 0.061 (the 300 um cell's bath at bolus size 100, 60 min per unit), and at most 0.0021 either way at bolus size 1. Unpaired fractions; Study 1 found at most about 10 to 13 points of paired net protection under held, saturating TNF.

With NF-kB intact, Apoptosis is on in more cells than NonACD at every held dose at 30 and 60 min per unit; at 120, and knocked out at every clock, NonACD is on in more at 6 to 8 of the 8 doses. Under held TNF cells are still dying at 24 h: up to 0.08, 0.10 and 0.15 of them die in the last 4 h at 30, 60 and 120 min per unit. In the fading baths at most 0.033 of the cells die in the last 4 h. At 30 min per unit the median time of first death is 3.3 to 6.8 h in the fading baths and 4.2 to 13.6 h in the held baths; at 120 it is 11.7 to 16.8 h in the fading baths.

The 54 matched fading baths (9 per arm and clock) leave 0.123 to 0.996 alive. Every bath at bolus size 1 leaves 0.960 to 0.996, and the 1000 um cell's bath at bolus size 10 leaves 0.966 at 120 min per unit in both arms: 20 of the 54 are within 0.05 of everyone alive, none within 0.05 of everyone dead. Decision 58 flags an E4 configuration near the ceiling when its distance side is too. These counts (alive_cells, cells) are the dose side of every E4 comparison.
findings.evidence: data/dose.json; e4_verdict.py reads its seeds and each bath's alive_cells and cells

findings.summary: NF-kB's first nuclear peak is the same at every clock and in both arms in each bath, as it must be. In the held baths it comes at 40.5 min (nuclear fraction 0.66) at occupancy 0.005 and no later at higher doses, 23.5 min (0.93) at occupancy 1; its height reaches 0.94 by occupancy 0.2. In the fading baths it comes at 23.5 to 38.5 min.
